How much does it cost to run a ceiling fan?

A typical ceiling fan uses about 50 watts (20–75W depending on the model). Used for 4 hours per day, 7 days a week, for 3 months of the year, it costs about 5.3p per day and £4.79 a year at the current price cap rate.

Cost per day
5.3p
About £4.79 a year at 4 hours per day, 7 days a week, 3 months a year.

Standing charge not included.

Adjust for yours
Ofgem price cap average for 1 Oct – 31 Dec 2026 (standard variable tariff, Direct Debit, England, Scotland & Wales).

About these figures

Source for the typical figure: Typical range (estimate). See how we calculate.

Ways to cut the cost

  • Run it on the lowest setting that does the job.
  • Close curtains on the sunny side during the day.
  • Use a timer so it isn't left running in an empty room.

Questions

How much does it cost to run a ceiling fan per hour?

At 26.32p/kWh, a 50W model costs about 1.3p an hour while it's running.

How much does it cost to run a ceiling fan per year?

About £4.79 a year, based on 4 hours per day, 7 days a week, 3 months a year. Change the sliders above to match how you use yours.

Is the standing charge included?

No. You pay the standing charge every day whether or not the appliance is used, so it isn't part of the cost of running it.

How do I find my ceiling fan's actual power use?

Check the rating label, plug or manual for the wattage, or the energy label for kWh figures. A plug-in energy monitor shows exactly what it uses.
